prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: authorized, traceable hospital dispensing/returns. Aliases/producers: Morrowglass=Medication Order Gateway—Order Reconciliation Snapshot; Cinderwake=Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot—Priority Refill Tote Tag; Juniper=Pharmacy Verification Station—Batch Release Note; Tallowmere=Medication Return Kiosk—Return Bin; Copperfield=Pharmacy Technician—Cold Chain Handoff Card; Bluejay=Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler; Larkspur=Registered Nurse; Stonewake=Biomedical Engineer. Other producers: Clinical Pharmacist—Dose Exception Review Slip; Hospital Courier—Pneumatic Capsule Seal Record; East Tube Dispatch Console—Tube Route Exception Ticket; Charge Nurse—Cabinet Downtime Notice; Medication Safety Officer—Diversion Review Packet. Morrowglass validates orders; invalid updates rejected/reasoned; unresolved/canceled/duplicate/superseded orders held. Cinderwake consumes Snapshot; reconciles identifiers/orders/dispenses/balances, cancellations/supersessions/duplicates/partials; preserves context/time; discrepancies audited/held; dispense inhibited without pharmacy authorization. Copperfield checks packaging/lot/expiry/cold-chain; reverifies delays; no dose decisions. Juniper final checkpoint: Clinical Pharmacist matches active order/product/strength/form/dose/route/time/patient/label; clarifies through Morrowglass. High-risk medications require recorded independent second check. Mismatches hold pending authorized resolution; approval records staff/time/medication identifiers. South Ward Cabinet Controller receives release note; applies approved configuration before compartment enablement. Larkspur confirms nonadministration/locks transactions; no bypass/substitution. Serious exceptions escalate. Medication Safety Officer reviews harm/diversion; IT Operations Specialist receives Packet/logs, no clinical changes; Stonewake assesses faults/restoration. Record disposition reviewer/evidence/outcome. Courier collects closed ready-recorded bins; manifests reconciled before Pneumatic Tube Network admission. West Tube Dispatch Console authorizes routing. East maintains approved map/availability; routes by destination/latest-approved version; checks reachability/interlocks/conflicts. Network reports segment-status/progress/delivery. Stale/incomplete status holds; sensor-communication loss means unavailable. Interruptions record capsule/location/time; stalled/unconfirmed delivery alerts Copperfield. Recovery requires refreshed status/approved route; route/temperature records retain time/equipment. North Ward Cabinet Controller uses approved location/product/threshold/role/transaction-limit configuration; authenticated roles; identity/location mismatch rejected; changes versioned/reviewed/approved; thresholds cannot override clinical

New part:
S205: The South Ward Cabinet Controller checks its local compartment mapping, access rules, and supported medication classes against that configuration.
S206: The cabinet reports Ready for Dispense only after its configuration checks and required device self-tests pass.
S207: The Registered Nurse authenticates at the cabinet and selects the medication associated with the active patient order.
S208: The South Ward Cabinet Controller checks the requested selection against its local authorization rules before unlocking a compartment.
S209: The cabinet records the user, order reference, compartment access, and transaction time for audit review.
S210: Stonewake reviews the received operational record, correlates its equipment identifiers and timestamps with local telemetry, and records an engineering disposition.
S211: The Biomedical Engineer uses the exception ticket to identify the affected path and compare reported symptoms with equipment telemetry.
S212: The Biomedical Engineer checks whether the reported condition is isolated to one device or indicates a broader service risk.
S213: When a hardware or control fault is suspected, the affected equipment is placed in Out of Service status.
S214: The Biomedical Engineer isolates the affected subsystem and performs only the diagnostic steps approved for that equipment.
S215: The IT Operations Specialist investigates authentication, interface, and time-synchronization faults that could affect transaction records.
S216: The Medication Safety Officer reviews any discrepancy that could change medication identity, access control, or patient risk.
S217: The Clinical Pharmacist keeps affected medication unavailable until the relevant order and product checks are repeated successfully.
S218: The Biomedical Engineer records the corrective action, test evidence, and approvals required to return the equipment to operation.
S219: Equipment remains Out of Service until required functional checks pass and the responsible staff approve its return.
S220: Audit records retain timestamps, equipment identifiers, and disposition details to support operational review and investigation.
S221: A cabinet outage is treated as a service incident when the cabinet stops responding, reports a fault, or fails a dispensing check.
S222: The IT Operations Specialist uses the Cabinet Downtime Notice to open a controlled incident record and identify the affected cabinet.
S223: The IT Operations Specialist checks controller status, network connectivity, and recent event logs before attempting recovery.
S224: The IT Operations Specialist records the time the fault was detected and the affected equipment identifier.
S225: The affected North Ward Cabinet Controller or South Ward Cabinet Controller remains Out of Service while the cause is assessed.
S226: The IT Operations Specialist isolates the fault where necessary to prevent repeated dispense requests from reaching an unavailable cabinet.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
